summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis was admitted for abdominal pain and possible gastrointestinal bleeding after reporting melena. Initial evaluation revealed stable hemoglobin and no active bleeding on EGD, which showed esophageal varices and portal gastropathy. She presented with mild hepatic encephalopathy, likely triggered by recent initiation of gabapentin and hydroxyzine, both of which were discontinued, leading to improved mental status. Abdominal pain was managed with tramadol and attributed to alcoholic gastritis or portal gastropathy. A known 2.6 cm hepatocellular carcinoma was confirmed, and outpatient TACE therapy was scheduled. Pancytopenia remained stable and was attributed to underlying cirrhosis and alcohol use. The patient was discharged home in improved condition with instructions to avoid alcohol, continue lactulose and rifaximin, and follow up with liver clinic and psychiatry.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C with hepatic coma
Esophageal varices without mention of bleeding
Alcoholic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage
Major depressive affective disorder, recurrent episode, unspecified
